prompt: Which Power Fx function returns only the records from a data source that match a condition, and on which gallery property do you set it?

options.text: Filter() — set on the gallery's Items property
Search() — set on the gallery's Default property
LookUp() — set on the gallery's Selected property
Patch() — set on the gallery's OnSelect property

explanation: Filter(DataSource, Condition) liefert nur die passenden Datensätze zurück. Gesetzt wird die Formel auf der Items-Eigenschaft der Galerie — sie bestimmt, welche Datensätze angezeigt werden.

source.title: Work with Power Fx formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: The Filter() function returns only the records from a data source that match a condition you specify. Set this formula on the Items property of a gallery to control which records appear.

prompt: You want to create a brand-new record with Patch(). What should you pass as the BaseRecord argument?

options.text: Defaults('Coffee Machines')
Gallery1.Selected
Blank()
LookUp('Coffee Machines', true)

explanation: Patch(DataSource, BaseRecord, ChangeRecord) legt an oder aktualisiert. Für einen neuen Datensatz übergibt man Defaults(DataSource) als BaseRecord — das liefert einen leeren Datensatz mit allen Standardwerten der Tabelle. Gallery1.Selected würde stattdessen den bestehenden Datensatz aktualisieren.

source.title: Work with Power Fx formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: Defaults(DataSource) returns a blank record with all default values for that table. Use it as the BaseRecord argument when creating new records rather than updating existing ones.

prompt: Match each Navigate() screen transition to its effect.

right.text: Slides new screen in from the side

explanation: Der zweite Parameter von Navigate() steuert die Animation: Slide schiebt den neuen Bildschirm seitlich herein (gut beim Vorwärtsgehen), Fade blendet weich um (unauffällig, richtungsneutral), None wechselt sofort (schnelle Navigation, Barrierefreiheit). Back() kehrt unabhängig davon immer zum Ursprungsbildschirm zurück.

source.title: Work with Power Fx formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: ScreenTransition.Slide Slides new screen in from the side Moving forward through a flow ScreenTransition.Fade Fades out and in Subtle, nondirectional changes ScreenTransition.None Instant switch, no animation Fast navigation or accessibility

prompt: In which property do you define a named formula so it can be referenced by name anywhere in a canvas app?

options.text: App.Formulas
App.OnStart
Screen.OnVisible
App.StartScreen

explanation: Named Formulas werden einmal in der Eigenschaft App.Formulas definiert und überall in der App per Name referenziert. Ändert sich der Wert — etwa eine Markenfarbe — passt man ihn an genau einer Stelle an, und alle referenzierenden Steuerelemente aktualisieren sich automatisch.

source.title: Build reusable components and formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: A named formula is a formula you define once in the App object and reference by name anywhere in your app, instead of rewriting the same logic in every control. Named formulas are defined in the App.Formulas property.

prompt: How do user-defined functions (UDFs) differ from named formulas in Power Fx?

options.text: It accepts parameters and returns a value, like a function in traditional programming
It is evaluated once when the app starts and its result is cached for the whole session
It is limited to returning Text values, while a named formula can return any data type
It must be defined in a component library before any screen can call it

explanation: Named Formulas liefern einen benannten Wert; User-defined Functions nehmen zusätzlich Parameter entgegen und geben einen typisierten Rückgabewert zurück — Syntax: FunctionName(Parameter1: Type): ReturnType = Expression. Beide werden in App.Formulas definiert. UDFs lohnen sich, wenn dieselbe mehrstufige Logik an mehreren Stellen auftaucht.

source.title: Build reusable components and formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: User-defined functions (UDFs) let you define a custom formula that accepts parameters and returns a value, similar to a function in traditional programming. UDFs are also defined in the App.Formulas property

prompt: How do component libraries differ from named formulas and user-defined functions?

options.text: They are visual building blocks with their own controls and properties, not just formula logic
They are restricted to model-driven apps, whereas named formulas work in canvas apps as well
They are limited to a single app and aren't shareable across the environment
They can be reused across apps but don't expose custom properties to the caller

explanation: Eine Component Library sammelt wiederverwendbare UI-Komponenten wie Header, Navigationsleisten oder Karten, die einmal gebaut und über mehrere Apps der Umgebung geteilt werden. Anders als Named Formulas und UDFs sind das visuelle Bausteine mit eigenen Steuerelementen, Eigenschaften und Verhalten.

source.title: Build reusable components and formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: Components are different from named formulas and UDFs: they're visual building blocks with their own controls, properties, and behaviors, not just formula logic.

prompt: What is the difference between saving and publishing a canvas app?

options.text: Saving stores changes without showing them to users; publishing pushes a new version live
Saving makes changes live immediately; publishing creates a restorable backup version
Saving and publishing are the same action, reached from two different buttons
Publishing stores a draft for review; saving releases the version to users

explanation: Speichern und Veröffentlichen sind zwei getrennte Aktionen: Speichern sichert den Arbeitsstand, ohne dass Nutzer die Änderungen sehen — wie ein Entwurf. Veröffentlichen bringt eine neue Version live, also die eigentliche Freigabe.

source.title: Publish your app
source.quote: When you save, you're capturing your work in progress — your changes are stored, but users running the app don't see them yet. When you publish, you push a new version live. Think of saving as committing to a draft, and publishing as releasing it.

prompt: For each of the following statements about sharing a canvas app, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: A user with the User permission can run the app but can't edit it or share it with others.
A co-owner can edit, share, and delete the app, but can't delete the original owner.
You must publish an app before you can manage its permissions and share it.

explanation: User dürfen die App nur ausführen, Co-Owner bearbeiten, teilen und löschen — aber nicht den ursprünglichen Besitzer entfernen. Berechtigungen lassen sich auch ohne Veröffentlichung verwalten und die App teilen, etwa zur Zusammenarbeit mit einem anderen Entwickler.

source.title: Share your app
source.quote: User — the person can run the app but can't edit it or share it with others. Co-owner — the person can edit, share, and delete the app. A co-owner can't delete the original owner. You can manage app permissions and share the app without publishing it, for example, if you want to collaborate with another developer.

prompt: When app-level security roles are enabled, Dataverse-backed apps show additional role options. Match each role to the access it grants.
explanation: Hat der Administrator App-Level-Sicherheitsrollen im Power Platform Admin Center aktiviert, steuern diese vier Rollen, was ein Nutzer in den zugrunde liegenden Dataverse-Tabellen lesen und schreiben darf — von reinem Lesezugriff (App reader) bis zum Vollzugriff auf alle Datensätze (App admin).

source.title: Share your app
source.quote: Dataverse-backed apps show additional role options: App reader (read-only access to all records), App user (full access to own records), App maker (create and read all records), and App admin (full access to all records).

prompt: How often does Power Apps save your work automatically by default, and where can you turn this off?

options.text: Every two minutes; under Settings > General > Auto save
Every 30 seconds; under Settings > Advanced > Save
Every 10 minutes; under Settings > General > Auto save interval
Only when you publish; there is no AutoSave option

explanation: Power Apps speichert standardmäßig alle zwei Minuten automatisch, damit bei einem unerwarteten Browser-Schluss nichts verloren geht. Ein- und ausschalten lässt sich das unter Settings > General > Auto save. Trotzdem gilt: vor dem Schließen des Tabs lieber manuell speichern.

source.title: Publish your app
source.quote: Power Apps saves your work automatically every two minutes by default. AutoSave helps prevent lost changes if your browser closes unexpectedly. You can turn AutoSave on or off in Settings > General > Auto save.

prompt: You use an Edit form control in a canvas app. Which function writes the record, and where do you typically navigate away after success?

options.text: SubmitForm(Form1) in the button's OnSelect; navigate in the form's OnSuccess
Patch() in the form's OnVisible; navigate in the button's OnSelect property
Collect() in the form's Items; navigate in the App.OnStart property
Filter() in the button's OnSelect; navigate in the screen's OnHidden

explanation: Bei einem Edit-Form-Steuerelement schreibt SubmitForm(FormName) den Datensatz — nicht Patch(). Der Aufruf gehört in die OnSelect-Eigenschaft der Speichern-Schaltfläche; nach erfolgreicher Übermittlung navigiert man über die OnSuccess-Eigenschaft des Formulars weiter.

source.title: Work with Power Fx formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: When you use an Edit form control, you write the record by calling SubmitForm() rather than Patch(). After a successful submission, you can navigate away automatically using the form's OnSuccess property

prompt: Complete the statement about passing the selected record to a detail screen.
textParts: You can pass data between screens using
, set as the third argument of Navigate(). Alternatively, setting the form's
property directly to Gallery1.Selected passes the selected record automatically.

options.text: context variables
named formulas
collections
Item
Items
Default

explanation: Navigate(DetailScreen, ScreenTransition.Slide, {SelectedMachine: Gallery1.Selected}) übergibt eine Kontextvariable an den Zielbildschirm. Einfacher geht es oft ohne: Setzt man die Item-Eigenschaft des Formulars direkt auf Gallery1.Selected, reicht Power Fx den ausgewählten Datensatz automatisch durch.

source.title: Work with Power Fx formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: You can do this using context variables. Alternatively, if you set the form's Item property directly to Gallery1.Selected, Power Fx automatically passes the selected record to the form, no context variable needed.

prompt: Which built-in Power Fx expression returns the display name of the currently signed-in user?

options.text: User().FullName
User().Email
CurrentUser.Name
Office365Users.MyProfile()

explanation: User().FullName liefert den Anzeigenamen des angemeldeten Nutzers, User().Email dessen E-Mail-Adresse. Damit lässt sich zum Beispiel eine Galerie auf die eigenen Datensätze filtern: Filter('Coffee Machines', 'Created By' = User().FullName).

source.title: Work with Power Fx formulas in canvas apps
source.quote: User().FullName is a built-in Power Fx expression that returns the display name of the currently signed-in user. User().Email returns their email address.

prompt: For each of the following statements about what users see when you publish an update, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: Users already running the app see two sequential notifications and select Refresh to load the new version.
These notifications appear when the app is embedded in Microsoft Teams, Power BI, or SharePoint form customizations.
In managed environments, Copilot can generate an app description automatically if you don't enter one before publishing.

explanation: Laufende Nutzer bekommen zwei Hinweise nacheinander und laden per Refresh die neue Fassung. Diese Benachrichtigungen erscheinen für Canvas-Apps im Web und in iframes — nicht aber bei Einbettung in Teams, Power BI oder SharePoint-Formularanpassungen. In Managed Environments erzeugt Copilot beim Veröffentlichen bei Bedarf automatisch eine Beschreibung.

source.title: Publish your app
source.quote: Users select Refresh to load the new version. These notifications appear for canvas apps on the web and in iframes, but not when the app is embedded in Microsoft Teams, Power BI, or SharePoint form customizations. If you don't enter a description before publishing, Copilot generates one automatically — you can always edit it afterward.
